_comment: Published reference values for scripts/validate-pk.ts. Every entry cites the sentence it came from. Rows may carry Cmax or tmax alone — the gate applies per metric and flags what is missing. no published reference is an honest outcome, not a gap to fill. Each metric carries its own quote: source_quote backs cmax (quoted in ng/mL, stored in mg/L — divide by 1000), tmax_quote backs tmax (quoted in hours). A comparator that is replaced is not deleted: it stays in withdrawn_tmax with its source and the reason, so a reviewer can see what changed and why.

references.cmax_note: observed mean ± SD 6255.10 ng/mL; treatment E (FDC oral, 1000 mg acetaminophen + 300 mg ibuprofen); converted ÷1000 to mg/L
references.source_title: Pharmacokinetics and Bioavailability of a Fixed-Dose Combination of Ibuprofen and Paracetamol after Intravenous and Oral Administration (Clin Drug Investig 2015;35:625-632)

citation_pack.publisher_values: Population-model predicted (fasted tablet, 1000 mg): Cmax 12.8 mg/L (95% PI 6.76-24.2), tmax 0.61 h (0.26-1.24)

references.tmax_note: Observed T max for treatment E (FDC oral, 1000 mg acetaminophen + 300 mg ibuprofen) — the same study, product, treatment arm and dose as the Cmax comparator above: 0.73 ± 0.42 h. The row is quoted verbatim in tmax_quote; the footnote marker a is not spelled out in the accessible text of the article, so the value is used as printed. The DailyMed Combogesic label (setid f863558f-2a44-41f8-a6b7-271851d4c2ff) states that peak plasma concentration following the administration of three COMBOGESIC tablets occurs at approximately 45 minutes and 1 hour 15 minutes after administration for acetaminophen and ibuprofen, respectively, under fasting condition — 0.75 h for acetaminophen, which agrees with the observed 0.73 h within rounding. Reviewed OpenCode source review, 2026-11-16.

withdrawn_tmax.source: DailyMed Combogesic label (setid f863558f-2a44-41f8-a6b7-271851d4c2ff): peak plasma concentration following the administration of three COMBOGESIC tablets occurs at approximately 45 minutes and 1 hour 15 minutes after administration for acetaminophen and ibuprofen, respectively, under fasting condition
withdrawn_tmax.reason: Superseded on 2026-11-16 by the observed value from the same study that supplies the Cmax comparator, so that both metrics of this record come from one study, product, treatment arm and dose. The label value agrees with the observed value within rounding (0.75 h vs 0.73 h) and is kept here.

references.cmax_note: observed mean ± SD 5178.29 ng/mL; treatment E (FDC oral, same combination product); converted ÷1000 to mg/L
references.source_title: Pharmacokinetics and Bioavailability of a Fixed-Dose Combination of Ibuprofen and Paracetamol after Intravenous and Oral Administration (Clin Drug Investig 2015;35:625-632)

citation_pack.publisher_values: Population-model predicted (fasted tablet, 300 mg): Cmax 24.1 mg/L (95% PI 13.3-40.8), tmax 0.94 h (0.48-1.67)

references.tmax_note: Observed T max for treatment E (FDC oral, 300 mg ibuprofen + 1000 mg acetaminophen) — the same study, product, treatment arm and dose as the Cmax comparator above: 1.49 ± 0.89 h. The row is quoted verbatim in tmax_quote; the footnote marker a is not spelled out in the accessible text of the article, so the value is used as printed. The DailyMed Combogesic label (setid f863558f-2a44-41f8-a6b7-271851d4c2ff) gives the same product a peak at approximately 1 hour 15 minutes after administration for ibuprofen under fasting condition — 1.25 h, the value the simulation reproduces. The population-model predicted tmax for a fasted 300 mg tablet (0.94 h, 95% PI 0.48-1.67) is in citation_pack, and the simulated value sits inside that interval. Reviewed OpenCode source review, 2026-11-16.

withdrawn_tmax.source: DailyMed ibuprofen suspension label (setid dda7645f-1666-4c1f-b974-01add2ea79ac): table legend T max (h) 0.79 (69%) 0.97 (57%)
withdrawn_tmax.reason: Withdrawn as the comparator on 2026-11-16. It is a different formulation (oral suspension) from the product the simulation models, its excerpt does not label which column each value belongs to, and the note recorded with it already said not to read 0.79 as a fasted-tablet reference. Kept here as a secondary, non-comparable number.

references.note: Arancibia 1980 (PMC283758) reports serum level SCHEDULES and rate constants (alpha 3.40/h, kappa a 1.02/h, ka absorption half-life 0.72 h) but no Cmax or tmax in the same source; no freely accessible published Cmax located. Do not fill from memory.

Tran 2017 (PMID 29018999) reports NLME parameters (ka 0.860/h, apparent CL/F 11.1 L/h, apparent V/F 81 L) but prints no observed or predicted Cmax or tmax in the abstract; not located in the accessible full text. Do not fill from memory. Label sweep (9d6def7) recorded t_max_h 0.75/0.79 for acetaminophen/ibuprofen; gabapentin tmax still not published in its source — unchanged.
Banwo 2024 (PMC11593559) and the DailyMed caffeine citrate label carry ka, F, CL and V but no published Cmax or tmax for a defined oral dose. Do not fill from memory.
